story.headline: Texas steamrolls UCLA, 55-20
body: Texas dominated from start to finish in a 55-20 rout over UCLA in Week 3 PCFL action, with Arch Manning earning Player of the Game honors after going for 27 of 40 for 378 yards and 5 TDs.
The Longhorns outgained UCLA 510–322 in total offense, including 137 yards on the ground. UCLA kept fighting, managing 322 total yards on the night.
Up next, Texas hosts Boston College in Week 4.

aiStory.headline: Manning's five touchdowns power Texas past UCLA 55-20
aiStory.dek: Texas moves to 3-0 atop the Eastern Atlantic while UCLA drops to 1-2 and falls two spots in the power poll.
body: Texas put the game away in the third quarter when Arch Manning hit Cam Coleman for a 2-yard touchdown at 11:54 to make it 31-14, then added two more Manning touchdown passes before the period ended to push the lead to 45-14. The Longhorns never looked back, closing with a Will Stone field goal and a late 29-yard Manning-to-Ryan Wingo strike for the final 55-20 margin.

Texas struck first on a 9-yard Quintrevion Wisner run and a successful two-point try for an 8-0 lead after one quarter. The Longhorns doubled the margin on a 7-yard Jerrick Gibson touchdown and two-point conversion before UCLA answered with a 4-yard Nico Iamaleava-to-Semaj Morgan strike. Manning then found Juan Davis for a 13-yard score and a two-point try to make it 24-7, but Iamaleava hit Leland Smith on a 68-yard bomb to pull UCLA within 24-14 at halftime. The third quarter belonged to Texas: Manning threw three more touchdowns — to Coleman, Michael Terry twice — and the lead ballooned to 45-14. A 24-yard Stone field goal and a late 29-yard Manning-to-Ryan Wingo connection closed the scoring at 55-20.

Texas outgained UCLA 510 yards to 322, dominating on the ground (137 to 15) and through the air (373 to 307). The Longhorns converted 67 percent of third downs (6 of 9) and held the ball for 33:25, exceeding their season average of 454 yards per game on offense. Manning finished 27 of 40 for 378 yards and five touchdowns, lifting his season totals to 902 yards and 12 scores with zero interceptions and a 129.6 rating. Gibson added 58 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries, bringing his season rushing total to 200 yards and the PCFL lead. UCLA's Iamaleava threw for 317 yards and three touchdowns, raising his season line to 963 yards and 13 touchdowns, but the Bruins managed only 15 rushing yards and turned the ball over on the critical muffed return.

Texas improves to 3-0 and remains the Eastern Atlantic division leader, though it slips from second to third in the power poll. UCLA falls to 1-2, drops from sixth to ninth in the poll, and sits third in the Western Pacific behind division-leading Washington. The Longhorns host Boston College (1-2) next week, while the Bruins travel to face Ohio State (1-2).
aiStory.turningPoint: Arch Manning's 2-yard touchdown pass to Cam Coleman at 11:54 of the third quarter extended the lead to 31-14 and began a run of three unanswered Texas touchdowns in the period.
byTheNumbers: Texas converted 6 of 9 third downs (67%) while UCLA went 7 of 15 (47%), extending drives and controlling tempo.
The Longhorns held a 137-15 rushing advantage, with Jerrick Gibson's 58 yards pushing his season total to a league-best 200.
Arch Manning threw five touchdowns without an interception, raising his season total to 12 and his rating to 129.6.
UCLA's only turnover — the muffed kickoff return by Kenneth Moore III recovered by Will Stone at 7:54 of the third quarter — gave Texas possession at the UCLA 34-yard line.

unsungHero.name: Will Stone
unsungHero.why: Recovered the muffed kickoff that gave Texas a short field in the third quarter and added a 24-yard field goal, contributing special-teams points and a critical turnover recovery.

aiStory.headline: Morris Caps Overtime Drive as Tennessee Outlasts Ohio State 35-29
aiStory.dek: The Volunteers stay perfect at 3-0 and atop the Eastern Southern while the Buckeyes fall to 1-2 and drop six spots in the power poll.
body: Overtime, third and less than four at the Ohio State seven, 8:09 on the clock — George MacIntyre drops back, finds Amari Jefferson crossing the end zone for a seven-yard touchdown, and Tennessee 35, Ohio State 29. The Volunteers had answered a 26-yard Jayden Fielding field goal with 16 seconds left in regulation by marching 79 yards in 1:37, MacIntyre hitting Joakim Dodson on a 40-yard strike and then a two-yard touchdown pass to knot it at 29, but the extra period belonged to the ground game: Tennessee ran the ball on every snap, grinding down to the seven before MacIntyre hit Jefferson for the winner.

Ohio State struck first, a 42-yard Fielding field goal at 13:40 of the first quarter, then Quinshon Judkins punched in a nine-yard run at 5:45 for a 10-0 lead. Tennessee answered with a 13-play, 73-yard drive, Morris scoring from two yards out and the two-point conversion good to make it 10-8 at 4:25 of the second. Fielding added a 33-yarder before halftime for a 13-8 Buckeye edge. A 39-yard Fielding kick pushed it to 16-8 at 9:14 of the third before MacIntyre found Braylon Staley on a one-yard touchdown and another two-pointer tied it at 16. Kyle Parker's 20-yard catch put Ohio State up 23-16 early in the fourth; Morris answered with a three-yard run at 6:31. Fielding's 45-yarder made it 26-23 at 3:07, then MacIntyre hit Dodson on a 40-yard bomb and a two-yard touchdown for a 29-26 Tennessee lead at 1:07. Fielding's 26-yarder with 16 seconds left forced overtime.

Tennessee won the yardage battle 446-351 and dominated time of possession 38:06 to 28:58, converting 9 of 14 third downs and all three fourth-down tries. MacIntyre threw for 346 yards and three touchdowns against two interceptions, pushing his season total to 1,071 yards — still the PCFL lead — while Travis Smith's 17-yard overtime catch lifted him to 392 receiving yards, also tops in the league. Morris, the Player of the Game, scored three touchdowns and keyed the overtime ground assault. Ohio State's Sayin passed for 259 yards and a touchdown with two picks, and Judkins managed just 29 yards on seven carries. The Buckeyes' five Fielding field goals kept them close, but two interceptions and zero fumble recoveries left them minus-two in turnover margin.

Tennessee improves to 3-0, holds the No. 1 power-poll spot and leads the Eastern Southern with a three-game win streak, averaging 32 points per game on offense and allowing 326.7 yards on defense — second in the league. Ohio State drops to 1-2, falls to No. 12 in the poll and sits third in the Western Central behind division-leading Notre Dame, having lost two straight while allowing 35 points and 370.3 yards per game on defense. Next week the Volunteers host Arkansas (2-1); the Buckeyes welcome UCLA (1-2) in a must-win for their division hopes.
aiStory.turningPoint: Overtime, 8:09 remaining, third and less than four at the Ohio State seven — MacIntyre's seven-yard touchdown pass to Amari Jefferson gave Tennessee a 35-29 lead that stood as the final margin.
byTheNumbers: Tennessee held the ball 38:06 to 28:58, converted 64% of third downs and was perfect on fourth down (3-for-3), wearing down an Ohio State defense that allows 370.3 yards per game.
MacIntyre's 346 passing yards pushed his season total to 1,071, maintaining the PCFL lead in passing yards.
Ohio State kicker Jayden Fielding made all five field-goal attempts (42, 33, 39, 45, 26 yards), providing 15 of the Buckeyes' 29 points.
Tennessee rushed for 105 yards on the night, with Daune Morris scoring three touchdowns, while Ohio State managed just 101 rushing yards and Quinshon Judkins was held to 29 yards on seven carries.

unsungHero.name: Jayden Fielding
unsungHero.why: He made all five field-goal attempts, including a 45-yarder and the 26-yarder that forced overtime, keeping Ohio State within striking distance despite the offense stalling in the red zone.

story.headline: Notre Dame takes control late, tops Georgia 41-28
body: Notre Dame asserted control when it mattered in a 41-28 win over Georgia in Week 3 PCFL action, with CJ Carr earning Player of the Game honors after going for 28 of 42 for 412 yards and 3 TDs.
The Fighting Irish outgained Georgia 551–361 in total offense, including 149 yards on the ground. Georgia kept fighting, managing 361 total yards on the night.
Up next, Notre Dame hosts Arizona State in Week 4.

aiStory.headline: Carr's 412-Yard Masterpiece Lifts Notre Dame Past Georgia 41-28
aiStory.dek: Notre Dame moves to 2-1 and atop the Western Central while Georgia falls to 0-3 and last in the Eastern Southern.
body: With 1:44 left in the fourth quarter and Notre Dame clinging to a 34-28 lead, CJ Carr stood at the Georgia 26 on first-and-10, scanned the field and delivered a strike to Golden Tate over the middle for a 26-yard touchdown that made it 41-28 and effectively sealed the game. The Irish offense had marched 83 yards in six plays over 1:32, the decisive blow coming after Carr hit Zayn Mcpherson for 32 yards to the Georgia 26 on the previous snap, turning a six-point edge into a two-score cushion with the clock ticking under two minutes.

The game opened with a methodical 14-play, 77-yard Notre Dame drive capped by Carr's short touchdown pass to Matt Jeffery at 7:10 of the first quarter, but Georgia answered quickly when Napoleon Lloyd punched in from close range at 3:59 to knot it at 7. Carr struck again early in the second, finding Xavier Southall for a 13-yard score and a 14-7 lead, only for TJ Giles to hit Rayhan Nash twice — from 13 yards at 7:47 and 10 yards at 0:57 — sandwiching a Darius Rivas field goal and giving Georgia a 21-17 halftime edge. Notre Dame seized control in the second half: Jadarian Price's one-yard plunge at 8:39 of the third put the Irish up 24-21, Rivas added a 38-yard field goal at 2:30 for a 27-21 lead, and Hollywood Smothers' six-yard touchdown run at 7:02 of the fourth — the culmination of a 12-play, 96-yard drive — stretched it to 34-21. Giles and Colbie Young connected on a five-yard score at 3:44 to pull Georgia within six before Carr's final dagger to Tate.

The box score tells the story of a lopsided battle in the trenches and on third down: Notre Dame outgained Georgia 551 yards to 361, dominated time of possession 38:59 to 21:01, and converted 7 of 12 third downs while the Bulldogs managed just 3 of 9. Carr was surgical at 28-of-42 for 412 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions, while Giles threw for 271 yards and three scores on 17-of-27 but could not sustain drives against an Irish defense that held Georgia to 93 rushing yards. Notre Dame's 149 rushing yards and 30 first downs reflected a balanced attack that kept the chains moving; the lone turnover — Mcpherson's fumble recovered by Travis Bates at 9:23 of the second quarter — did not translate into points for Georgia, as Reggie Willis missed a 39-yard field goal on the ensuing possession. Carr's 412 yards lead all PCFL quarterbacks through three weeks, and his 32.3 points-per-game average now paces a Notre Dame offense ranked fifth in the league at 440.3 yards per game, while Georgia's defense remains last at 498.3 yards allowed per game.

Notre Dame improves to 2-1, climbs to No. 4 in the power poll and takes sole possession of the Western Central lead with a two-game winning streak heading into a home matchup against Arizona State (1-2). Georgia drops to 0-3, slips to No. 17 in the poll and sits last in the Eastern Southern, three games behind division leader Tennessee, with a home date against Miami (1-2) next on the schedule. The Bulldogs' offense, 18th in the league at 314.7 yards per game, showed flashes — Jimmy Campbell's 61-yard burst and Colbie Young's 108 receiving yards — but the defense's inability to get off the field on third down and the 17-minute possession deficit proved fatal against a Carr-led attack that now averages 41 points over its last two outings.
aiStory.turningPoint: Carr's 26-yard touchdown pass to Golden Tate at 1:44 of the fourth quarter turned a six-point lead into a 13-point margin and ended Georgia's comeback hopes.
byTheNumbers: Notre Dame converted 58% of third downs (7/12) versus Georgia's 33% (3/9), extending drives and chewing 38:59 of clock.
Carr threw for 412 yards — the highest single-game total in the PCFL this season — on 28-of-42 with three touchdowns and zero interceptions.
Georgia managed only 93 rushing yards on the day, while Notre Dame's 149 ground yards and 30 first downs sustained a 96-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter.
The lone turnover — Mcpherson's fumble at 9:23 Q2 — led to a missed 39-yard field goal by Willis, leaving four points off the board for Georgia.

unsungHero.name: Darius Rivas
unsungHero.why: He made both field-goal attempts — a 19-yarder in the second quarter and a 38-yarder in the third — providing six crucial points in a game decided by two scores.

aiStory.headline: Nussmeier Finds Hasty in Overtime as LSU Escapes Michigan 30-24
aiStory.dek: The Tigers improve to 3-0 and climb to No. 2 in the power poll while the Wolverines fall to 1-2 and tumble to No. 12.
body: Overtime, 1:58 remaining, first and goal at the Michigan 4: Garrett Nussmeier drops back, scans the middle of the field and fires a dart to Woody Hasty for a four-yard touchdown that puts LSU ahead 30-24 and ultimately ends the game. Michigan had seen two field-goal attempts from Herbie Swanson miss — a 19-yarder wide and a 51-yarder short — and their overtime possession ended with those misses.

LSU struck first on a methodical 11-play, 80-yard opening drive capped by Tim Ferguson's one-yard plunge for a 7-0 lead. Michigan answered with Calvin Wendtland's three-yard score to tie it at 7, then LSU reclaimed the lead on Yousef Snow's 11-yard run. Eric Brock's four-yard touchdown knotted the score at 14 before Lilian Munoz's 29-yard field goal made it 17-14 at halftime. The Tigers pushed the margin to 10 on Mason Taylor's 29-yard catch in the third quarter, but Michigan rallied with Vance Boyer's one-yard reception and Swanson's 48-yard field goal to force overtime at 24-24.

The box score tells a story of two evenly matched offenses: Michigan outgained LSU 456-442 and held a 212-178 edge on the ground behind Wendtland's 99 yards, while Nussmeier threw for 275 yards and two scores to pace a 264-yard aerial attack. Third-down efficiency was nearly identical at 43% for LSU and 41% for Michigan, and each team recorded one interception in the play-by-play — Jakailin Johnson picking off Chip Gabriel in the second quarter and William Jackson intercepting Nussmeier in the third. Penalties were minimal at one apiece, and time of possession was virtually even. Nussmeier's 22-of-38, 275-yard, two-touchdown line lifts his season totals to 691 yards, seven touchdowns and a 101.1 rating, ninth in the PCFL in passing yards. Wendtland's 99 yards on nine carries pushes his season total to 189 yards at 9.4 per carry, second in the league.

The win moves LSU to 3-0 and vaults the Tigers from No. 4 to No. 2 in the power poll, keeping them in the hunt atop the Eastern Southern behind division leader Tennessee. Michigan drops to 1-2 and slides from No. 6 to No. 12, now chasing Notre Dame in the Western Central with a loss already on the ledger. Next week the Tigers host Penn State (1-2) while the Wolverines travel to face winless Michigan State.
aiStory.turningPoint: Overtime, 1:58 — Nussmeier's four-yard touchdown pass to Hasty on first and goal gave LSU a 30-24 lead that held after Michigan's two missed field goals.
byTheNumbers: Michigan outgained LSU 456-442 but converted only 7 of 17 third downs (41%) and went 0-for-1 on fourth down, including a failed 4th-and-3 at the LSU 27 in the third quarter.
Nussmeier's 275 passing yards and two touchdowns raised his season total to 691 yards and seven scores, placing him ninth in the PCFL in passing yards.
Wendtland's 99 rushing yards on nine carries (11.0 avg.) pushed his season average to 9.4 yards per carry, second in the league behind only Jerrick Gibson.
Swanson missed two overtime field goals (19 yards wide, 51 yards short), leaving six points on the board in a six-point game.

unsungHero.name: Jakailin Johnson
unsungHero.why: His second-quarter interception of Gabriel gave LSU possession and preceded the field goal that made it 17-14 at halftime.

aiStory.headline: MacCormick's Three Touchdowns Power Boston College Past Colorado
aiStory.dek: Boston College snaps an 0-2 start while Colorado drops its second straight to fall below .500.
body: With 1:35 left in the fourth quarter and Boston College clinging to a 32-23 lead, Sam Leavitt handed off to Bo MacCormick on third-and-3 from the Colorado 6. MacCormick burst through the line for a 6-yard touchdown run, pushing the advantage to 39-23 and effectively sealing the Eagles' first victory of the season.

Boston College struck first on a 12-play, 80-yard opening drive capped by MacCormick's short touchdown run and a successful two-point conversion for an 8-0 lead. Colorado answered with a 47-yard field goal, but Darius Rivas' 48-yard field goal restored an eight-point edge. The Buffaloes closed the half on Roger Anderson's 9-yard touchdown pass to Jimmy Horn Jr., trimming the deficit to 11-9. Leavitt found Nedrick Bolden for a 12-yard score on the first drive of the third quarter to make it 18-9. Anderson hit Matthew Golden from 12 yards out early in the fourth to pull Colorado within 18-16, then Leavitt connected with Jordon Mcdonald for a 19-yard touchdown. A short field set up Mike Van Horne's 3-yard run to bring Colorado back to 25-23, but MacCormick added two more rushing touchdowns in the final five minutes to put the game away.

The box score tells the story of control: Boston College outgained Colorado 450 yards to 210, rushed for 126 yards against just 14, and converted 50 percent of third downs while holding the ball for nearly 35 minutes. Leavitt completed 27 of 43 passes for 324 yards and two touchdowns without a turnover, while Anderson threw for 227 yards and two scores on 18-of-43 passing. MacCormick's 59-yard catch on a pass from Leavitt in the fourth quarter set up his second touchdown and left Colorado safety Julius Lawson seriously injured. Defensively, Boston College's Collins recorded two sacks and the Eagles forced three failed fourth-down attempts by Colorado, including two in the final quarter.

The win lifts Boston College to 1-2 overall and moves the program up two spots to No. 12 in the power poll, though the Eagles remain third in the Eastern Atlantic behind division leader Texas. Colorado falls to 1-2 and slides six places to No. 16, dropping to fourth in the Western Central behind Notre Dame. Boston College heads to unbeaten Texas next week, while Colorado returns home to face 2-1 Alabama.
aiStory.turningPoint: MacCormick's 6-yard touchdown run on third-and-3 with 1:35 remaining in the fourth quarter extended Boston College's lead to 16 points and ended Colorado's comeback hopes.
byTheNumbers: Boston College dominated time of possession 34:46 to 25:14, sustaining drives and limiting Colorado's offensive opportunities.
The Eagles converted 7 of 14 third downs (50%) while Colorado went 0-for-2 on fourth down in the fourth quarter alone.
Boston College rushed for 126 yards compared to Colorado's 14 yards, controlling the line of scrimmage.
Leavitt's 324 passing yards pushed Boston College's offense to 450 total yards, well above its season average of 365.7.

unsungHero.name: Collins
unsungHero.why: Recorded two sacks and two tackles, providing pressure that helped limit Colorado to 210 total yards.

aiStory.headline: Arkansas routs Penn State 41-18 behind Trotter's three touchdowns
aiStory.dek: Arkansas jumps to 2-1 and #4 in the power poll while Penn State falls to 1-2 and drops to #12 heading into a road test at unbeaten LSU.
body: With 2:00 left in the fourth quarter and Arkansas leading 34-18, Cade Trotter found Laurence Wright on an 11-yard strike from the Penn State 11 to make it 41-18 and put the game out of reach.

Penn State struck first on a 47-yard Yousef Joseph field goal at 9:33 of the first quarter, but Arkansas answered with a Braylon Russell touchdown run to lead 7-3. The Nittany Lions reclaimed the lead at 10-7 on a Madison Jenkins plunge with 2:11 left in the half, only for Trotter to hit Wright for a 42-yard score with 47 seconds left in the second quarter and a 14-10 Arkansas edge at the break. Trotter opened the third quarter with a 13-yard touchdown to Caden Ochoa and Cruz Gibson added a 31-yard field goal for a 24-10 cushion. Gibson hit a 41-yarder early in the fourth, Penn State cut it to 27-18 on a 25-yard Myers-to-Edwards touchdown and a successful two-point try, then Mike Washington broke a 56-yard touchdown run and Trotter found Wright again to seal the 23-point final margin.

The box score tells the story: Arkansas turned 408 yards into 41 points while Penn State's 401 yards yielded just 18, a gap explained by Arkansas's perfect 2-for-2 fourth-down conversion rate versus Penn State's 2-for-4 and a critical Myers interception returned 42 yards by Theo Walker at 3:41 of the fourth. Trotter was surgical at 15-of-25 for 232 yards and three touchdowns, Wright caught six passes for 140 yards and two scores, and Washington added 83 yards and a touchdown on just five carries. For Penn State, Myers threw for 338 yards and a touchdown on 50 attempts but the lone pick and two failed fourth downs — including one at the Penn State 48 early in the fourth — stalled drives; Edwards led all receivers with 119 yards and a score on six catches.

Arkansas improves to 2-1, vaults from #10 to #4 in the power poll and sits third in the Eastern Southern division behind 3-0 Tennessee, who visit next week. Penn State drops to 1-2, slides to #12 and falls to the bottom of the Eastern Atlantic at 1-2 with a two-game skid, now facing a road trip to 3-0 LSU.
aiStory.turningPoint: Trotter's 11-yard touchdown pass to Wright at 2:00 of the fourth quarter extended the lead to 41-18 and ended any comeback hope.
byTheNumbers: Arkansas converted both fourth-down attempts while Penn State went 2-for-4, including a failed 4th-and-short at the Penn State 48 at 14:12 of the fourth quarter.
Penn State held the ball for 35:16 but managed only 18 points on 401 total yards.
Trotter threw three touchdowns with zero interceptions on 25 attempts; Myers threw one touchdown with one interception on 50 attempts.

story.headline: Arizona State survives Washington by 1 in thriller
body: Arizona State found just enough in a 35-34 thriller over Washington in Week 3 PCFL action, with Brock Thomas earning Player of the Game honors after going for 19 of 27 for 273 yards and 5 TDs.
The Sun Devils outgained Washington 364–345 in total offense, including 109 yards on the ground. Washington kept fighting, managing 345 total yards on the night.
Up next, Arizona State travels to face Notre Dame in Week 4.

aiStory.headline: Thomas throws five TDs as Arizona State edges Washington 35-34
aiStory.dek: The Sun Devils snap an 0-2 start while the Huskies drop their first game and cling to the Western Pacific lead.
body: With 2:36 left and Arizona State clinging to a 35-34 lead, Brock Thomas hit Ryan Pellum for 7 yards on third-and-short at the Sun Devils' 39, moving the chains and letting the offense bleed the clock down to a punt that pinned Washington at its own 20 with one minute remaining.

Arizona State struck first when Thomas found Cooper Perry for a 5-yard score at 11:13 of the first quarter, then doubled the lead to 14-0 on a 66-yard catch-and-run by Makhi Hughes early in the second. Washington answered twice before halftime — Demond Williams Jr. hit Rashid Williams from 12 yards out, then Brian Bonner Jr. punched in from three — to make it 14-13 at the break. The Huskies surged ahead 20-14 on Jordan Washington's short touchdown run to open the third, but a Mason James fumble recovered by Ify Obidegwu flipped the field, and Thomas threw two quick touchdowns to Aaron Bidwell and Vander Ploog for a 28-20 Arizona State lead. Williams Jr. and Rashid Williams connected again from 11 yards to pull Washington within 28-27, Thomas answered with an 11-yard strike to Pellum for 35-27, and Jayden Limar's 3-yard run with 4:14 left set up the final margin.

The box score tells the story of two offenses that moved the ball at will: Washington rolled up 345 yards (199 passing, 146 rushing) and converted 10 of 14 third downs, while Arizona State countered with 364 yards (255 passing, 109 rushing) but managed only 3 of 9 on third down. The decisive difference was ball security — Washington lost one of three fumbles, the costly third-quarter muff by James that set up a Sun Devils touchdown, while Arizona State put the ball on the ground zero times. Thomas delivered the Player of the Game line, 19 of 27 for 273 yards and five touchdowns, pushing his season total to 35 points per game for a unit that entered averaging 25. Williams Jr. threw for 179 yards and two scores and added a rushing touchdown, while Rashid Williams caught nine passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns, lifting his season receiving to 233 yards and third in the PCFL. Limar chipped in 63 yards on six carries with a score, averaging 7.9 yards per attempt for the year.

Washington falls to 2-1 and slips from fourth to sixth in the power poll, though it remains atop the Western Pacific at 2-1 with a one-game lead. Arizona State improves to 1-2, jumps from 14th to ninth in the poll, and snaps its losing streak heading into a road test at Notre Dame. The Huskies host USC next week looking to regain their footing on defense, which allowed 35 points after entering the game yielding 27 per contest.

byTheNumbers: Third-down efficiency: Washington 71% (10/14) vs. Arizona State 33% (3/9) — the Huskies sustained drives but the Sun Devils struck on big plays.
Turnover margin: Washington 1 lost fumble, Arizona State 0 — the lone takeaway produced 7 points for the Sun Devils.
Brock Thomas 5 touchdown passes on 27 attempts — 18.5% of his throws reached the end zone, turning a 33% third-down rate into 35 points.
Rashid Williams 9 catches, 92 yards, 2 TDs — moved to 233 receiving yards on the season, fourth in the PCFL.

unsungHero.name: Ify Obidegwu

body: Miami found just enough in a 34-28 win over USC in Week 3 PCFL action, with Graham Mertz earning Player of the Game honors after going for 41 of 67 for 418 yards and 2 TDs.

aiStory.headline: Lilly's 18-yard overtime dash lifts Miami past USC 34-28
aiStory.dek: Miami snaps an 0-2 start and climbs to 1-2 while USC drops its first game and falls to 2-1 in the Western Pacific race.
body: Overtime, 7:25 on the clock, third-and-8 at the USC 18: Graham Mertz handed to Colby Lilly, who burst through the left side and raced 18 yards for the winning touchdown, making it Miami 34, USC 28 and ending a seesaw night that had already produced four fourth-quarter lead changes.

Miami struck first at 10:42 of the second quarter when Mertz hit Ernie Simmons on a 9-yard score and the two-point conversion made it 8-0. USC answered twice before halftime — Miller Moss to Connor Burnett from 13 yards, then Moss to Patrick Farthing from 8 yards — to take a 14-8 lead. Vencie Sites' 24-yard field goal cut it to 14-11 at the break. Sites added a 44-yarder at 2:09 of the third to tie it at 14. USC surged ahead 21-14 on Raleigh Montgomery's 3-yard plunge at 9:59 of the fourth, but Romeo Dixon's 3-yard run at 6:42 knotted it again. Rodney Linville's 6-yard touchdown put USC up 28-21 at 4:02, only for Mertz to find Chimere Dike on a 12-yard strike with 41 seconds left to force overtime at 28-all.

The box score tells the story: Miami outgained USC 488-394, powered by Mertz's 41-of-67, 418-yard, two-touchdown effort that pushed his season total to 1,030 yards — second in the PCFL behind Tennessee's Geor MacIntyre (1,071). USC's Moss threw for 315 yards and two scores but the Trojans managed just 97 rushing yards on 32 carries, while Miami's ground game, though only 80 yards total, delivered the overtime winner. Third-down efficiency favored USC (60% to 50%), yet Miami converted all three fourth-down attempts and won the turnover battle when Jack Williams intercepted Moss at the Miami 31 on the first overtime possession. Lilly's 57 yards on five carries included the decisive 18-yarder; his season average now sits at 7.5 yards per carry, ninth in the league. USC's defense, allowing 430.3 yards per game (14th in the PCFL), couldn't contain Miami's 408 passing yards.

USC falls to 2-1 and slips from No. 2 to No. 6 in the power poll, now second in the Western Pacific behind Washington with a home date against the Huskies next week. Miami improves to 1-2, jumps from No. 14 to No. 9, and rides a one-game winning streak into a road trip to Georgia (0-3) looking to climb out of the Eastern Southern basement.

byTheNumbers: Miami 488 total yards vs. USC 394 — the Hurricanes' 408 passing yards overwhelmed a USC defense ranked 14th in the PCFL at 430.3 yards allowed per game.
Miami 3-for-3 on fourth down vs. USC 0-for-0 — every fourth-down conversion extended drives that produced points, including the overtime possession.
Zero Miami turnovers vs. one USC interception — Jack Williams' pick in overtime flipped the field and ended USC's opening overtime drive.
Colby Lilly 5 carries, 57 yards, 1 TD (18-yard overtime winner) — his 7.5 yards-per-carry season average ranks ninth in the PCFL.

unsungHero.why: Made both field-goal attempts (24 and 44 yards) and the game-tying extra point after the fourth-quarter touchdown, providing the only points of the first half for Miami and keeping the Hurricanes within striking distance.

aiStory.headline: Cortez, Fields Strike Early; Spartans' Late Rally Falls One Point Short
aiStory.dek: Alabama moves to 2-1 and second in the Eastern Atlantic while Michigan State drops to 0-3 and last in the Western Central.
body: With 25 seconds left and Michigan State trailing 28-21 at the Alabama 3, Arnold Glass found Anthony Andrel on a slant for a 3-yard touchdown to make it 28-27, but Keith Rocha's extra point was blocked by Emmett Belser and recovered by Asa Benton, sealing a one-point escape for the Crimson Tide.

Alabama struck twice in the opening quarter, James Cortez hitting Terrill Fields for a 61-yard score at 14:05 and Merv Salo for a 37-yarder at 1:28 to lead 14-0. A 39-yard Rocha field goal cut it to 14-3 before Cortez capped a 12-play, 77-yard drive with a 2-yard keeper for a 21-3 halftime edge. Glass answered with a 60-yard strike to Jason Walsh and an 8-yard dart to Andrel in the third quarter to pull within 21-18, but Cortez and Fields connected again on a 17-yard touchdown early in the fourth for a 28-18 cushion. Rocha's 47-yarder made it 28-21 with 3:29 left, setting up the final drive that ended on the blocked PAT.

The box score tells the story of two aerial attacks: Glass threw for 374 yards and three touchdowns on 31-of-47 passing, while Cortez was 27-of-37 for 388 yards and three scores, pushing his season total to 943 yards and fourth in the PCFL. Michigan State outgained Alabama 413-397 but managed only 42 rushing yards to the Tide's 21, and the third-down gap — 57 percent for Alabama versus 38 percent for the Spartans — kept drives alive for the home side. The lone turnover, a Toi Bernard fumble recovered by Carlos Hinton at the Alabama 26 with 13:46 remaining, gave Alabama the ball in a one-score game; the Tide later punted with 1:55 left, giving Michigan State the chance for the final march.

Alabama improves to 2-1 with a win that follows a loss, climbing from 10th to sixth in the power poll and sitting second in the Eastern Atlantic behind Texas. Michigan State falls to 0-3, its power-poll ranking slipping from 14th to 17th while remaining winless in the Western Central. The Spartans host Michigan next week; the Crimson Tide travel to Colorado.

Turnover margin: Michigan State lost its only fumble (Bernard, Q4 13:46) while Alabama had zero giveaways, denying the Spartans a possession in a one-score game.
Passing volume: Glass (374 yards) and Cortez (388) combined for 762 yards through the air, with Cortez moving to fourth in the league with 943 yards on the season.
Red-zone finish: Michigan State settled for two field goals and needed a fourth-down conversion on the final drive; Alabama scored touchdowns on three of four trips inside the 20.

unsungHero.name: Emmett Belser
unsungHero.why: The defensive tackle blocked the potential game-tying extra point with 19 seconds remaining, preserving the one-point victory.

weeklyWrap.headline: Three Overtimes and a Power Poll Shake-Up Define Week 3
weeklyWrap.subhead: Tennessee, LSU, and Miami survive extra frames while Arkansas and Notre Dame crash the top four.
weeklyWrap.lead: Week 3 delivered three overtime thrillers and a seismic shift at the top of the power poll, where Tennessee, LSU, and Texas remain the only unbeatens. Arkansas vaulted six spots to tie Notre Dame at No. 4 after a 41-18 dismantling of Penn State.

segments.title: Tennessee Outlasts Ohio State in Overtime
segments.body: Ohio State led 10-0 after one quarter and 13-8 at halftime before Tennessee forced a 29-29 deadlock after four quarters. The Volunteers won 35-29 in overtime in a game that featured five turnovers and a single lead change.

segments.title: LSU Survives Michigan in Extra Time
segments.body: LSU never trailed, leading 17-14 at halftime and holding a 24-14 edge after three quarters, but Michigan rallied to knot the score at 24-24. The Tigers answered in overtime with a six-point finish to stay perfect at 3-0.

segments.title: Miami Stuns USC in Overtime
segments.body: A scoreless first quarter gave way to a back-and-forth affair that saw Miami erase a 14-11 halftime deficit and force overtime tied at 28. The Hurricanes then put up six unanswered points in the extra period to hand USC a loss that dropped the Trojans to 2-1.

segments.title: Arkansas and Notre Dame Crash the Top Four
segments.body: Arkansas surged from No. 10 to a share of No. 4 after a 41-18 rout of Penn State that featured a 23-point maximum lead. Notre Dame joined them at No. 4 following a 41-28 win at Georgia in which the Irish outscored the Bulldogs 24-7 in the second half.

segments.title: Texas, Tennessee, LSU Stand Alone at 3-0
segments.body: Texas blew the doors off UCLA with a 24-point second quarter en route to a 55-20 victory, joining Tennessee and LSU as the league's only undefeated teams. The Longhorns never trailed and forced one turnover while building a 35-point maximum lead.

weeklyWrap.closer: Next week puts the unbeaten trio on high alert as Tennessee, LSU, and Texas each face ranked opponents with playoff positioning already on the line.
